Original events.proof: An event-only decoder must choose one label per render class. It can correctly cover at most the largest label mass in that class; the saved majority-label lookup attains this. Sum those maxima and divide by the declared total mass. Randomization cannot improve zero-one expected accuracy.
Original events.scope: Exact optimum under the declared finite input prior and exact events, with no input identity, dates, numeric labels or other side information. Uniform distinct-input weights are a chosen analysis assumption, not observed population frequencies. Weighted priors are caller declarations, not estimated probabilities. Joint score requires all listed answers correct together. Zero-weight inputs do not affect accuracy, so perfect accuracy does not certify their recoverability. No source authenticity, human accuracy, hearing model, training benefit or held-out generalization claim.

lower_bound.scope: Exactly one pitch event per sample, fixed onset and duration, no other data-bearing channel. Bound follows from distinct singleton answer vectors.

partition.scope: All positive-length series of real values in the declared closed interval, no missing samples. Monotone nonuniform bins, inclusive threshold boundaries, original pitch vocabulary and fixed timing retained. Each event preserves every requested threshold predicate, hence occurrence indices and counts as well as any/all decisions. Event-level sufficiency only; no human listening claim or numerical-value recovery.
partition.reason: Every requested nonconstant threshold is a bin boundary; the construction attains the scoped alphabet lower bound

scope: Same declared finite domain, prior and answers for every candidate. Pareto axes are ideal joint accuracy (maximize), weighted playback duration and count of pitches used in that domain (minimize). These chosen engineering axes are not measured cognitive load, audibility, aesthetic quality or a recommendation. Source mapping is shared; candidate representation rules may change.
